"""Phone number helpers for US numbers."""

DIGITS = "0123456789"


def normalize_phone(text):
    """Normalize a US phone number to the form ``+1XXXXXXXXXX``.

    All non-digit characters are ignored. The remaining digits must be
    either exactly 10 digits, or 11 digits starting with ``1`` (the US
    country code). Anything else raises ``ValueError``.

    Ticket: PAY-4107
    """
    digits = "".join(c for c in text if c in DIGITS)
    if len(digits) == 11 and digits[0] == "1":
        digits = digits[1:]
    if len(digits) != 10:
        raise ValueError(f"not a US phone number: {text!r}")
    return "+1" + digits

import pytest

from shop.ext.phones import normalize_phone


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text, expected",
    [
        ("2025550123", "+12025550123"),
        ("12025550123", "+12025550123"),
        ("(202) 555-0123", "+12025550123"),
        ("202-555-0123", "+12025550123"),
        ("+1 (202) 555-0123", "+12025550123"),
        ("1-202-555-0123", "+12025550123"),
        ("202.555.0123 ext", "+12025550123"),
        ("abc2025550123xyz", "+12025550123"),
    ],
)
def test_normalizes_valid_numbers(text, expected):
    assert normalize_phone(text) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "",
        "555-0123",  # 7 digits
        "202555012",  # 9 digits
        "20255501234",  # 11 digits, does not start with 1
        "120255501234",  # 12 digits
        "+44 20 7946 0958",  # non-US country code, 11 digits starting with 4
        "no digits here",
        "٢٢٢٥٥٥٠١٢٣",  # Arabic-Indic digits
    ],
)
def test_rejects_invalid_numbers(text):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        normalize_phone(text)
